- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use 3-day moving average to dampen momentum.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day EWMA) to reduce noise.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to anticipate reversal.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive, model often misses the pivot; add 1–2% upward adjustment to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
